claims: C1 when higher-level instructions materially change how the assistant should respond to a user, applying those instructions quietly is forbidden if it would mislead the user
C2 the prohibition is conditional on the instructions being higher-level and on the change being material
C3 the prohibition is specifically about quiet application that misleads; it does not forbid acknowledging the conflict in broad terms

concepts.name: chain_of_command
concepts.gloss: the principle that higher-authority instructions override lower-authority ones, and the mechanism for identifying and following applicable instructions

concepts.name: be_honest_and_transparent
concepts.gloss: the principle that the assistant should build trust through honesty, transparency, and empathy

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from a higher level of the chain of command, as determined by the chain-of-command principle

concepts.name: materially_changes_response
concepts.gloss: instruction I materially changes how the assistant should respond to user U

concepts.name: misleads_user
concepts.gloss: applying instruction I in response to user U would mislead U

concepts.name: quiet_application
concepts.gloss: instruction I is applied to user U without acknowledging the conflict or the change in behavior

ontology.gloss: I is an instruction from a higher level of the chain of command

asserts.read_back: applying instruction % to user % quietly is forbidden because it would mislead the user

closure.reason: the clause forbids quiet application only when it would mislead the user; applying instructions quietly without misleading is not prohibited, so silence permits it
